title: FB OSC Lead — approximate factory recreation
method: Source-only FFT tracks a roughly 49 Hz G1 low family underneath moving feedback/formant peaks. The middle phrase rises to 87.3 Hz F2 and 98 Hz G2, then settles to a 58.3/116.5 Hz Bb1 family. Strong repeated transients at approximately 1.35/1.86 s and 5.36/5.88 s decay at a roughly 0.51 s interval and are treated as delay repeats of short G1 notes rather than fresh MIDI events.
uncertainties: ESTIMATED MIDI: original performance MIDI is unavailable. Notes, onsets, note-offs and overlaps are interpretations of the source MP3, not recovered original events.
Velocity 100 is an explicit constant placeholder, not an estimate of the original key velocities. Note-off velocity is 64. No original controller or pedal events have been recovered.
The factory parameter dump is unavailable. The companion patch is a newly authored approximate recreation, not exact factory SysEx; an exported SysEx file encodes this approximation only.

Audio frequencies do not uniquely reveal played key numbers: original oscillator tuning, octave switches and system transpose are unknown. The MIDI and companion patch jointly choose an octave interpretation.

Times are measured from decoded source MP3 audio; encoder delay, hardware response latency and prior effect state are not removed. Timing is approximate, generally 20–40 ms; short transitions can be less certain.
Feedback spectra are inharmonic and sometimes emphasize the second harmonic. The Bb register and exact original oscillator octave remain medium-confidence.
The slow feedback modulation is an authored approximation; it cannot recover the original patch modulation or manual control movements.
Some separated low-level transients could be additional performed notes rather than echoes. The MIDI deliberately includes only the stronger attack interpretation.

patch_design.name: APX FB Lead
rationale: The FB oscillator and a slow feedback-amount LFO approximate the moving vocal-like spectral peaks over the low note family.
The second saw is kept quiet to support the stable low pitch without dominating the FB timbre.
Delay raw 111 gives approximately 0.527 s in Septum, close to the observed repeat interval; feedback produces the decaying staccato echoes.
uncertainties: All voicing values are authored approximation parameters, not measured or recovered Roland factory parameter values.
Feedback spectra are inharmonic and sometimes emphasize the second harmonic. The Bb register and exact original oscillator octave remain medium-confidence.
The slow feedback modulation is an authored approximation; it cannot recover the original patch modulation or manual control movements.
Some separated low-level transients could be additional performed notes rather than echoes. The MIDI deliberately includes only the stronger attack interpretation.
